quiz.title: Equivalent Simplifying and Comparing Fractions Quiz
quiz.instructions: Choose one answer for each question. For simplification questions, use the simplest form. For ordering questions, work from smallest to largest.

questions.working:
The denominator is multiplied by 4, so multiply the numerator by 4 as well.

\(2\times4=8\), so \(\frac{2}{3}=\frac{8}{12}\).

Divide the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor, 6.

\(\frac{12}{18}=\frac{12\div 6}{18\div 6}=\frac{2}{3}\).

Divide the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor, 5.

\(\frac{15}{35}=\frac{15\div 5}{35\div 5}=\frac{3}{7}\).

Divide the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor, 8.

\(\frac{24}{40}=\frac{24\div 8}{40\div 8}=\frac{3}{5}\).

Divide the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor, 14.

\(\frac{42}{56}=\frac{42\div 14}{56\div 14}=\frac{3}{4}\).

questions.prompt: Choose the symbol that makes this statement true: \(\frac{3}{4}\;\square\;\frac{5}{8}\).
questions.working:
Write both fractions with denominator 8.

\(\frac{3}{4}=\frac{6}{8},\qquad \frac{5}{8}=\frac{5}{8}\).

Compare the numerators: \(\frac{3}{4}\gt\frac{5}{8}\).

questions.prompt: Choose the symbol that makes this statement true: \(\frac{5}{6}\;\square\;\frac{7}{8}\).
questions.working:
Write both fractions with denominator 24.

\(\frac{5}{6}=\frac{20}{24},\qquad \frac{7}{8}=\frac{21}{24}\).

Compare the numerators: \(\frac{5}{6}\lt\frac{7}{8}\).

questions.prompt: Put these fractions in order from smallest to largest: \(\frac{3}{4},\;\frac{1}{2},\;\frac{2}{3}\).
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 12:

\(\frac{3}{4}=\frac{9}{12},\quad \frac{1}{2}=\frac{6}{12},\quad \frac{2}{3}=\frac{8}{12}\).

From smallest to largest: \(\frac{1}{2},\;\frac{2}{3},\;\frac{3}{4}\).

questions.prompt: Put these fractions in order from smallest to largest: \(\frac{7}{10},\;\frac{3}{5},\;\frac{2}{3}\).
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 30:

\(\frac{7}{10}=\frac{21}{30},\quad \frac{3}{5}=\frac{18}{30},\quad \frac{2}{3}=\frac{20}{30}\).

From smallest to largest: \(\frac{3}{5},\;\frac{2}{3},\;\frac{7}{10}\).
